700650701.text: Well, well. If it isn't our great master of anti-self-termination, Josephus. So, why are you here, cursing all who live?

700650702.text: Cut it out. Nobody dies in the Temple of Space.

700650703.text: How strange. Did you try testing that rule, Sir Anti-Self-Termination?

700650704.text: Keep talking, and a new batch of guards will be on its way.

700650705.text: Alright. Special times call for special treatment. I won't make fun of you.

700650706.text: #{NICKNAME}, Zeitlind. This is Josephus. He's a friend of mine.

700650707.text: No need to be so sentimental. Everyone here is everyone else's friend.

700650708.text: If you can't come to love or be loved by everyone over such long periods of time, you'd drown the world in sorrow.

700650709.text: Come. Let us set our course for the heart of the world. A realm not reserved for the old or the dead, for the rich or poor.

700650710.text: Hehe, I've quoted that poem before.

700651501.text: "Maukie"... Paimon feels like she might've heard that before...

700651502.text: Ach. No, no. This isn't the time for that either.

700651503.text: Let me ask you, do any of you have combat strength on par with a junior Remurian Centurion or higher?

700651504.text: #Don't worry, {NICKNAME} can beat people up just fine.

700651505.text: Come on, then. Let's head out and show them what Pankration, or maybe Machaira, means to you.

700650801.text: It's safer here. I don't know why, but the suppression-type guards can't get in.

700650802.text: Organization-type Keepers usually don't harm people either. Unless you try to steal relics, that is.

700650803.text: Zeitlind, you've been gripping that suitcase this whole time. Your knuckles are all pale.

700650804.text: It's safe here, so just put it down for now, 'kay?

700650805.text: Well, unless you've got stolen relics in that suitcase. But that can't be, right?

700650807.text: Still, Paimon's sure it's gotta be full of valuable items.

700650808.text: Not really. Just some things I needed to say goodbye to before leaving.

700650811.text: You and your sister have vastly different personalities.

700650813.text: Ah... I mean... Have you... met my sister? Did she come here before? So the "Hilda" you mentioned before really is...

700650814.text: Easy now, young Zeitlind. This place is safe. We can take our time talking about your sister.

700650815.text: Shameless fellow. Hilda called you Grandpa.

700650816.text: I couldn't tell you how many years ago I was born. Still, I have heard you all speak of an age long past, when the gods waged war across the land.

700650817.text: In my time, there were no gods living in our lands at all. Have you ever seen an angel?

700650818.text: That makes you a great-great-great-great grandpa, Grandpa Istoria!

700650819.text: Nay, nay. Once you get here, all are caught within stagnant space-time. Saints and commoners, wise and foolish, young and old. There is no difference.

700650820.text: That is to say, don't call me Grandpa.

700650821.text: Then let's call each other whatever we want. I'll call you "Grandpa Istoria," and you can call me "young Hilda."

700650822.text: She was a good lass. But for some reason, she always looked a little gloomy.

700650824.text: Hey, stop getting sentimental! Zeitlind's suitcase has been stolen!

700650826.text: It got away. This is going to be a difficult chase.

700650828.text: Don't let this get you down, Zeitlind. I have a theory.

700651003.text: Looks like we've only recovered a small part of Lind's stuff, though.

700651004.text: Then it's as I suspected. Your suitcase and everything inside it have been classified as relics of this age.

700651005.text: The rest were likely dispersed and placed in other areas.

700651006.text: Don't worry, Zeitlind. We'll find them together.

700651008.text: Then, shall I tell you about the themed areas?

700651011.text: Besides people like us, some landscapes, relics, and even ecosystems were also uplifted to this place.

700651012.text: The temple was originally meant to preserve them as segments of human culture, though some gradually developed their own functions.

700651013.text: Take, for example, the Luyang Academy from ancient Liyue. It has now become an area devoted to art and painting.

700651014.text: Then there's Venipi, a laborer who once hauled stone for The Mausoleum of King Deshret. Under orders, he rebuilt a desert style complex called the Desert Pavilion.

700651015.text: Last is my personal favorite, the Mahavaipulya Chamber. Besides ancient texts, it also contains new novels written by some of the uplifted.

700651016.text: But since the purpose of the Temple of Space is preservation rather than evolution, they were also the first to face punishment.

700651017.text: So if we go to those three places, we can find the things Zeitlind lost, right?

700651018.text: You could also free those areas and rescue the others. If it's not too much trouble, of course.

700651019.text: Oh ho, Istoria. That's gonna run you extra.

700651020.text: I wouldn't put it like that. We should go help everyone *and* find my things along the way.

700651021.text: Your personal effects are of utmost importance here, Lind. You are, after all, someone who lives in the present.

700651022.text: This place is but an anthology of the past. It has no future, whereas you still have yours.

700651023.text: That makes your needs the most important. Do you understand?

700651024.text: In the end, a living person may amount to nothing more than a name on gravestone.

700651025.text: Even so, a name carries countless memories, as well as the stories and strength passed on through them, young Zeitlind.

700651026.text: Let us return and rest for now. I suspect you still have many questions.

700651201.text: A cursed mountain where none who enter ever return...

700651202.text: Um, what exactly are we looking for?

700651203.text: Maybe a note. A scrap of paper... Or perhaps just traces of a life that once existed here.

700651204.text: With the demolition already this far along, there may not be much left to find. Still, I have to try.

700650201.text: And that's how it happened — I swear it on my paycheck, and the responsibilities that come with it.

700650202.text: Weren't you bemoaning how little you make as a doorman?

700650203.text: I'm not just any doorman. I oversee demolition work and cultural heritage preservation.

700650205.text: Though yeah, the pay is bad... Well, then I swear it on my reputation at the tavern.

700650206.text: A most serious oath for us Mondstadters.

700650207.text: I should really investigate this myself, but I still have to meet up with the Knights' expedition, who are returning to Dornman Port...

700650208.text: #Sorry about this, {NICKNAME}, but could you check out the sanatorium for me?

700650209.text: Ugh, kinda-sorta scary stories like this usually mean something bigger's at play.

700650210.text: Then what about super scary stories?

700650211.text: The truth behind those is usually... Uh... basic scientific facts about how superstition can be harmful.

700650212.text: It's fine. I know my way around a fight either way.

700650213.text: Eh, true. We've run into ghosts before, too. Most of them were actually pretty easy to talk to.

700650214.text: So there really are ghosts in this world?

700650215.text: No, no. It's all just strange elemental powers and scientific phenomena at work.

700650216.text: In that case, I won't go today. I'll just stay in Dornman Port and have some drinks.

subQuests.subQuestName: Head to the sanatorium on the mountain

700650501.text: Ah, yes. Come, come, it's team huddle time. We've a strategy meeting to hold.

700650503.text: Ooh, Paimon almost forgot. Istoria, do you know how to send someone back down to the ground?

700650505.text: Then can you tell us how to send Zeitlind back? She's just an ordinary person.

700650506.text: In the past, that would have been nearly impossible. But the temple's laws and order draw close unto collapse, making it now a trivial matter.

700650507.text: You simply need to do me a small favor.

700650508.text: Hmm, alright, but it better be small.

700650509.text: Oh, it's simple. Smash a few crappy guards, rescue an old friend, and escort us back to the center of the Pillar Hall.

700650511.text: #And do you know what kind of god rules this place? {NICKNAME} is looking for her.

700650512.text: This was once the sacred hall of the God of Space. But she is nowhere to be found.

700650513.text: After the mistress vanished, one of the two stewards fell from grace and departed.

700650514.text: The one who remained, Melanta, grew increasingly severe with us. He did not descend into the mortal world, but he has descended into madness.

700650515.text: Melanta? Does that mean that the one who fell from grace is that self-absorbed Nihilita guy?

700650516.text: Correct. The Watcher who introduced Dex to you is one who departed. Nihilita of Nothingness.

700650517.text: Hah, so it really was that big-winged guy who talks to himself, doesn't care what people say, and changes the subject whenever you ask him uncomfortable questions!

700650518.text: Huh. Does he really talk that much?

700650519.text: *sigh* No matter. The two of them were once divine familiars who watched over the world from the Pillar Hall of Space.

700650520.text: The Temple of Space selects people and objects from a specific historical age or a now-vanished civilization, using them as the smallest possible segments.

700650521.text: Once elevated, the chosen are preserved here as living memories, forever.

700650522.text: That doesn't sound like a very happy fate.

700650523.text: I suspect it was not originally designed as an eternal paradise or some heaven in the sky.

700650524.text: Still, the God of Space's sisters would occasionally bring things of interest into the temple and grant small pardons for acts of change.

700650525.text: Oh, Paimon gets it. This place was a spotless but dull bookshelf that the sisters then covered in stickers and stuffed with light novels.

700650526.text: Then Melanta, driven by longing for his creator, reversed all the rules to their original form. He began purging everything that had changed, punishing anyone who broke from precedent.

700650527.text: I gathered the courage to leave the relative safety of the temple's center, hoping I might be able to save an old friend.

700650528.text: But my lack of Pankration training caught up with me, and I ended up getting chased by the guards and hiding in that spot earlier.

700650529.text: Alright. That's the introduction. What's our plan?

700650530.text: We fight our way through and save anyone we know.

700650531.text: Fine. Looks like Melanta's the highest up the ladder we can reach for now. Hopefully, we can get some answers from him.

700650601.text: It's as we thought. There's nothing in the graveyard.

700650602.text: Old Mann must've made a mistake...

700650603.text: Still, look at the portrait on this grave. This girl was so young... There's a sad story behind this one for sure.

700650604.text: Are you friends of my sister too?

700650608.text: Uh, so, you've gotta be the younger sister of the person buried here, right?

700650609.text: Well, are you also her friends?

700650611.text: You scared the old man at the gate last night, so the Knights sent us to investigate.

700650612.text: I see. Well, I'm just here to look for her. I didn't expect that rumor to be true.

700650614.text: That "those who go to the sanatorium will stay there," or something similar.

700650615.text: In her letters, my sister said the sanatorium was about to close, and that she was going somewhere far away.

700650616.text: Um... M—Maybe she went traveling around the world or something?

700650617.text: No wait. Her gravestone is right here... Sorry.

700650618.text: It's alright. Before I came, I thought the same way you did. It took me some time to prepare myself before I could come here for answers.

700650619.text: I might have arrived a bit too late last night and ended up frightening the old man.

700650620.text: Please help me pass along my apology. I'm sorry for causing all this trouble.

700650621.text: It's okay. Paimon totally gets you. Just gotta explain it to everyone, and you'll be fine.

700650634.text: It was a little late last night. I'd planned to ask the old man about the situation, but he fled without even looking back.

700650622.text: For now, I want to look for traces of how she lived her life. Perhaps that would lead us to some clues on... why she would...

700650623.text: Y'know what? Let us help you. It's getting late, and the sooner we finish, the sooner we can head down the mountain.

700650625.text: By the way, what's your name?

700650628.text: Wh—What is it? Is it an, uh, embarrassing name or something?

700650629.text: In that case, Paimon can, uh, give you a nickname... How's that sound?

700650630.text: No. It's just... I had planned to... Well, I came to say goodbye.

700650633.text: #Alright then. Let's help Zeitlind look around together, shall we, {NICKNAME}?

700651701.text: There's so much dust on the bed. It must've been meant for sanatorium patients back in the day, right?

subQuests.subQuestName: Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister
Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister

700651603.text: Mm. I'm fine. My sense of time's a bit off, though. Like a very long while has passed, and yet also just an instant.

700651604.text: That sounds like a familiar feeling.

700651606.text: You must've been through plenty of misfortune, too. How long has it been for you, then?

700651608.text: What? Has so much time passed already?

700651609.text: #Oh, no. {F#She's}{M#He's} talking about the time-weirdness stuff that happened to {F#her}{M#him}.

700651610.text: That said, Paimon's not sure if "five hundred years" is that accurate at this point either.

700651611.text: As for this time, it's only been about ten minutes or so?

700651612.text: Huh. So that's how long it's been?

700651615.text: You never asked us for our names.

700651616.text: Ah, yes. When I tried to call for help just now, I realized I didn't even know what to call you.

700651617.text: Sorry. At first, I was planning to... Well, never mind.

700651618.text: #I already know that you're {NICKNAME}. What about your pet?

700651619.text: #Hey! Paimon's not a pet! Paimon's {NICKNAME}'s best guide and companion!

700651621.text: And if you're gonna make another corny joke, you can stuff it.

700651624.text: We'll make sure you get back down safely. But for now, we don't have any leads as to how.

700651625.text: So let's keep moving forward. We need to find someone and ask them what's going on.

700650301.text: Zeitlind, were you waiting for us here?

700650302.text: No. I think... Something feels off...

700650303.text: Uh... was that always so far away?

700650304.text: Huh? This place looks kinda different from before.

700650307.text: I am Nihilita, Watcher of Nothingness, the Open-Eyed.

700650308.text: Noble traveler from distant realms, returnee from the sea of stars... Greetings. I bid you welcome.

700650311.text: As it should be. We dwell within the watchtowers of the world. We were never meant to meet, even across countless ages.

700650312.text: Yet I have now fallen into the mortal realm, for one purpose alone. I beg that you ascend to the high heavens and free the Aiones of the past from their inverted fates.

700650313.text: Please, touch the Anemo Archon's statue over there. It is a gateway that leads unto the heavens.

700650314.text: Wait! Can't you see that there's an ordinary person here?

700650315.text: Are you sure Zeitlind is supposed to hear these things? At least let us take her back first!

700650319.text: Please remain calm. I merely placed her under my protection, so that she shall not suffer any apathic afflictions after ascending.

700650320.text: So, you mean we're bringing Zeitlind with us?

700650321.text: She has her own journey to embark upon. When you reach the temple above the sky, she will be restored.

700650322.text: Hey, hold on! We never agreed to go to some strange place like that. Let Zeitlind out first!

700650323.text: This is not some strange place. It is the seat of governance above the skies. Its name is "Segment-Domain Tau." Or perhaps, let us use its lost name.

700650327.text: That is correct. It belongs to the god who once appeared before you, my creator. Within the temple, you shall find your answers.

700650328.text: Please take this with you. It will aid you in my stead.

700650332.text: Uh, could you explain what it actually is!?

700650333.text: A Watcher does not explain. A Watcher observes, in silence.

700650334.text: Once safety may be guaranteed, it will restore Zeitlind.

700650335.text: Don't just assume that we're going! You're just looking to dump responsibility for this onto someone, aren't you?

700650336.text: Noble outlander, are you willing to go?

700650337.text: There it is again, talking to yourself and dodging the question. You haven't been making any sense for a while now, y'know?

700650338.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you know what it's trying to say?

700650342.text: Okay, sure. If that's what you want, then Paimon will go with you.

700650344.text: If my earlier discourtesy has stirred anger within you, come at me with blade in hand. I will await you in the mortal world.

700650101.text: Some people just won't listen. I already told you, now's not the time to go up the mountain.

700650102.text: Easy there, Old Mann. Let's calm down and talk this out.

700650103.text: We were getting along just fine earlier at the Night Brew.

700650104.text: But the moment I mentioned I was heading for Windrest Peak, he grabbed me and dragged me all the way here.

700650105.text: Oh, Huffman. What's going on here?

700650106.text: As you can see, Old Mann is trying his best to keep people away from Windrest Peak.

700650107.text: Anyway, let me introduce you. This is Lipphart, an adventurer.

700650108.text: What I saw... What I felt... It was terrifying! Surely you don't wish to hear it?

700650109.text: Doesn't look like I'm going anywhere today, so let's hear it. Consider it an extension of our drinking and bragging session from earlier.

700650110.text: So, what sort of "great peril" are we facing here?

700650111.text: The sanatorium's haunted! Seriously! I saw them ghosts with my own eyes!

700650402.text: Huh!? Humans...? I thought the "uplifting" had already ended. More cases like Hilda's, then?

700650403.text: No, wait. Perhaps you were simply unlucky. Newcomers who have only recently passed the trial of the Apathic Interval, maybe?

700650404.text: Greetings, newcomers. My name is Istoria. I hail from the age when the Dark Dragon King rent the sky open. And you are?

700650410.text: Ah. Dexter. You are here as well!

700650411.text: Now I understand. You must be people of the present age. In which case, you have come to reinforce us!

700650413.text: Also, Dex's real name is Dexter, huh? Is it your friend?

700650414.text: No. We call it Dex too. But it just sent me a secret signal.

700650415.text: As such, I introduced it using the more official, more impressive-sounding name.

700650416.text: #Hey, Hey, {NICKNAME}. Paimon wants a formal name and a secret code, too.

700650417.text: Ah, but now is not the time for such talk.

700650418.text: Since Nihilita has sent you up here, that means it is finally our time to strike back.

700650419.text: Wait a minute! We're still confused.

700650420.text: How confused? More confused than I was the first time I looked upon Escher's paintings?

700651301.text: E...scher? As in, Escher the Engineer?

700651302.text: Does the name ring a bell? He's from a very long time ago, though. Surely not someone you know...

700651303.text: Eh, you know what? Who knows. Maybe he really was famous. Actually, that pisses me off. Why didn't I make my mark in history?

700651304.text: You know what? Let's just call him "Maukie" from now on.

700651403.text: His family calls him "Maukie", and so do we.
